This is strong, multi-source, primary-document evidence for a double-counted row, not merely the pre-existing roster suspicion restated.

concerns.researcher_notes:
ORCHESTRATOR ADJUDICATION 2026-09-14 — this SUPERSEDES the duplicate verdict this shard's row agent reached, and the matching verdict in the other row's shard. P3200 and P5990 are NOT the same project. They are two SUCCESSIVE, separately-filed Virginia Natural Gas applications to the Virginia SCC, and GEM has recorded them under the same name:
  (a) HEADER IMPROVEMENT PROJECT (HIP) — ~24 mi in three distinct pipelines: the 6.2 mi Transco Interconnect Pipeline (Quantico to Transco's mainline at Catlett, Fauquier Co), the 3.3 mi Quantico Parallel Pipe (Fauquier Co), and the 14.6 mi Mechanicsville Parallel Pipe (Hanover, New Kent and Charles City Cos) = 24.1 mi; ~$346M; 30 in. Sized for the proposed C4GT gas-fired plant in Charles City County, which supplied the bulk of the project's funding. DISMISSED by the Virginia SCC in December 2020 after VNG told the Commission the C4GT conditions would not be met by the Dec 31 deadline. => This is the project P5990's DATA describes (24 mi / 30 in / $346M / Prince William-Fauquier, and both of P5990's own live-sheet refs are Header-Improvement-Project pages).
  (b) VNG INTERCONNECT — the renamed, downsized successor, filed 2020-12-14, three days before HIP's dismissal took effect. ~10 mi (about 6 mi in Prince William Co + 4 mi in Fauquier Co), i.e. HIP's first two segments (6.2 + 3.3 = 9.5 mi) with the 14.6 mi Mechanicsville leg DROPPED; +245,000 Dth/d (~245 MMcf/d); $205M; plus a new compressor station near Nokesville and upgrades to the Hanover/Mechanicsville metering station. WITHDRAWN March 2021 as 'no longer needed as proposed'. => This is the project P3200's DATA describes, and it is EIA's single 'VNG Interconnect' row (Aug 2026, sheet 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)', Excel row 1143: 10 miles, 245 MMcf/d, $205M, VA, authority SCC).
The two scopes OVERLAP physically (the Interconnect re-proposes HIP's two northern segments) but they are separate applications with separate dockets, separate scopes, separate costs and separate dispositions, and EIA carries only the second. Merging or retiring either row would delete a real, separately-adjudicated project from the record. KEEP BOTH. The defects are naming and attribution, not duplication.

concerns.recommendation: NOT a duplicate - keep both rows, and do NOT retire P3200. concerns.researcher_notes:
ORCHESTRATOR ADJUDICATION 2026-09-14 — this SUPERSEDES the 'CONFIRMED DUPLICATE' verdict this shard reached and the retire-P3200 recommendation in its cross_row_leads. The row agent's PROJECT HISTORY was right and is adopted in full; only the direction of the fix is reversed.
P3200 and P5990 are NOT the same project. They are two successive Virginia Natural Gas applications to the Virginia SCC:
  (a) HEADER IMPROVEMENT PROJECT (HIP) — three new 30-inch pipelines totalling ~24 mi (Transco Interconnect Pipeline 6.2 mi + Quantico Parallel Pipe 3.3 mi + Mechanicsville Parallel Pipe 14.6 mi = 24.1 mi), ~$346M, across Prince William, Fauquier, Hanover, New Kent and Charles City counties, sized for the proposed C4GT plant in Charles City County. DISMISSED by the SCC in December 2020 once C4GT's conditions could not be met.
  (b) VNG INTERCONNECT — the renamed, downsized successor filed 2020-12-14: ~10 mi (about 6 mi Prince William + 4 mi Fauquier, i.e. HIP's two northern segments with the 14.6 mi Mechanicsville leg dropped), 245 MMcf/d, $205M, plus a compressor station near Nokesville and Hanover metering upgrades. WITHDRAWN March 2021. This is EIA's single 'VNG Interconnect' row (Aug 2026, sheet 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)', Excel row 1143).
THIS ROW (P5990) HOLDS HIP'S DATA, NOT THE INTERCONNECT'S: 24 mi, 30 in, $346M, Prince William to Fauquier — and BOTH of its live-sheet refs are Header-Improvement-Project pages (Chesapeake Climate's 'Header Injustice Project' page; the Bay Journal's report of the SCC's Dec 1 2020 dismissal). P3200 holds the Interconnect's data (10 mi, 245 MMcf/d, $205M) and matches EIA.
THEREFORE THE DEFECT ON THIS ROW IS ITS NAME, NOT ITS NUMBERS. The row agent proposed the opposite — rewriting LengthKnown down to ~10 mi and SegmentCost down to $205M to match the name. That is rejected: it would make P5990 a second copy of P3200 and delete the Header Improvement Project — a real, separately-filed, separately-dismissed project — from the database entirely, while overwriting correctly-sourced values with another project's figures. KEEP BOTH ROWS; KEEP THIS ROW'S 24 mi / 30 in / $346M; CHANGE THIS ROW'S NAME.

concerns.researcher_notes: ADJUDICATED: P0146 (Alaska Pipeline Project) and P0174 (Denali - The Alaska Gas Pipeline) are TWO GENUINELY COMPETING PROPOSALS, not one physical project entered twice. Two independent origins say so explicitly. (1) Office of the Federal Coordinator, arcticgas.gov: 'Denali-The Alaska Gas Pipeline, a joint venture of North Slope producers ConocoPhillips and BP, was established in April 2008 TO COMPETE WITH the TransCanada project ... In May 2011, Denali announced it would no longer pursue development.' (2) CRS R40963: 'the State of Alaska's 2008 award to TransCanada ... and the concurrent announcement of a COMPETING pipeline proposal, the Denali project, by BP and ConocoPhillips. Through 2010, the Denali and TransCanada pipelines were proceeding along similar tracks. However, in May 2011, Denali's developers announced the discontinuation of their pipeline project'. They differ on every axis that identifies a project: SPONSORS (TransCanada + ExxonMobil vs BP + ConocoPhillips); REGULATORY VEHICLE (AGIA license awarded Dec 2008 + FERC pre-file Docket PF09-11-000 vs a non-AGIA proposal with its own separate FERC pre-file); CAPACITY as proposed (CRS: TransCanada 4.5-5.0 Bcf/d; Denali 4.0 Bcf/d); SCOPE (Denali always included its own gas treatment plant, the AGIA project initially did not); and END DATE (Denali withdrew May 2011; APP's prefile docket was terminated 26 Aug 2014). They shared an origin (Prudhoe Bay), a corridor (the Alaska Highway route to Alberta) and a rough design scale, which is why the rows look alike. CAVEAT and the reason this is not a clean 'none': P0146's Capacity and Length [ref] cells currently cite a Hart Energy article about DENALI's cancellation - a cross-row misattribution that made the two rows look like one. Both are re-pointed to APP-specific sources in fills[]. A second-order concern for P0174 (raised as a cross-row lead, not edited here): CRS states Denali was a 4.0 Bcf/d proposal, while GEM carries 4,500 MMcf/d on that row, so the identical capacity that prompted the duplicate suspicion may itself be an artifact of the same misattribution.

concerns.recommendation: no merge - keep P0147, P0293 and P6534 as separate rows; record P6534 as an AKLNG component and P0293 as the abandoned rival in-state plan
concerns.researcher_notes: DUPLICATE ADJUDICATION for the Alaska cluster, which the brief flags as easy to conflate. (1) P6534 Point Thomson Unit Gas Transmission Pipeline (63 mi, 32-inch, 865 MMcf/d) IS part of the same FERC application but is NOT a duplicate of P0147 - it is a physically distinct feeder line. The FERC order authorises, as separate facilities, '62.5 miles of 32-inch-diameter pipeline on the North Slope, which will [run] from the Point Thomson Unit gas production facility to the Prudhoe Bay Treatment Plant (Point Thomson Unit Gas Transmission Line)' and '1.0 miles of 60-inch-diameter pipeline ... (Prudhoe Bay Unit Gas Transmission Line)', alongside the 806.9-mile Mainline. Resource Report No. 1 gives the Point Thomson line its own specs - 62.5 mi, 32-inch, 865 MMSCF/D average stream day rate, 920 MMSCF/D peak, MAOP 1,150 psig - which match P6534's sheet values exactly, so P6534 is correctly and independently recorded. The relationship should be NAMED (P6534 is AKLNG's Point Thomson lateral; Glenfarne's Phase One 'may also include the 63-mile, 32-inch Point Thomson Lateral Pipeline'), and P0147's 807 mi must stay Mainline-only so the two rows do not double-count. Note also that the 60-inch, 1-mile Prudhoe Bay Unit line appears to have no GEM row at all. (2) P0293 Alaska Stand Alone Pipeline (ASAP) is NOT the same project as P0147 and has not been folded into AKLNG Phase One, despite sharing a sponsor (AGDC), a corridor and a North-Slope-to-Southcentral purpose. EIA's Historical Projects sheet keeps ASAP as its own row with different physical specs - 737 mi, '12,36' inch, 500 MMcf/d, $9,970M, status 'On Hold' - and describes it as 'a buried in-state natural gas pipeline ... considered to be the backup plan to the Alaska LNG project', terminating at 'the ENSTAR system near Point Mackenzie in the Mat-Su Valley', not Nikiski. AKLNG Phase One is a 739-mile 42-inch line under FERC docket CP17-178 held by 8 Star Alaska LLC; ASAP is a separate, dormant state project. Different diameter, different capacity, different terminus, different authorisation - two rows, correctly. (3) P0146 Alaska Pipeline Project (TransCanada/ExxonMobil, FERC PF09-11) and P0174 Denali (BP/ConocoPhillips, FERC PF08-26) are 1,126-1,700 mile Alaska Highway export lines to Alberta from an earlier era, already adjudicated as distinct in their own shards; nothing in AKLNG's record folds either into P0147, and I have not merged anything.

concerns.recommendation: Keep P0174 and P0146 as SEPARATE rows - do not merge; they are rival consortia, not one project
concerns.researcher_notes: ADJUDICATION of the P0174-vs-P0146 duplicate hypothesis raised by the orchestrator: they are NOT the same project. They are the two genuinely competing 2000s-era Alaska Highway proposals, and the evidence is regulatory, not inferential. (1) SEPARATE FERC DOCKETS, described side by side in separate sections of the SAME document: FERC's ANGTA Eleventh Report to Congress (Feb 2011) has 'B. Denali's Proposal ... Denali plans to construct and operate a gas treatment plant (GTP) near Prudhoe Bay and a 48-inch-diameter pipeline to transport up to 4.5 Bcf/d from the Alaska North Slope to the Alberta Hub ... Docket No. PF08-26-000' and, immediately following, 'C. TC Alaska's Proposal ... Docket No. PF09-11-000'. A regulator does not open two pre-filing dockets for one project. (2) SEPARATE SPONSORS: Denali = BP plc + ConocoPhillips (50/50 JV incorporated as Denali - The Alaska Gas Pipeline LLC, announced 2008-04-08); the Alaska Pipeline Project = TransCanada/TC Energy + ExxonMobil, built on TransCanada's 2008 AGIA licence from the State of Alaska. Denali's own filing acknowledges TransCanada's separate AGIA licence. (3) SEPARATE OPEN SEASONS, months apart: TC Alaska's closed 2010-07-30, Denali's closed 2010-10-04. (4) SEPARATE ENDINGS: Denali withdrew from pre-filing 2011-05-17 (ANGTA Twelfth Report); the APP continued and is recorded on P0146 as cancelled in 2014. (5) DIFFERENT PHYSICAL SCOPE: the ANGTA Twelfth Report describes the APP as 'a gas treatment plant (GTP) near Prudhoe Bay, about 58 miles of 32-inch-diameter pipeline from the processing plant at the Point Thomson Field to the GTP, and about 745 miles of 48-inch-diameter mainline pipeline from the GTP to the Alaska-Yukon border', versus Denali's 730-mile Alaska Mainline + 1,020-mile Canada Mainline to Blueberry Hill, AB. (6) The trade press treats them as rivals throughout: AP (2010-04-07) frames Denali's open season against the competing TransCanada/Exxon project, and NGI (2011-05-23) quotes TransCanada VP Tony Palmer on Denali - 'They're an independent project'. The shared 4,500 MMcf/d is not a duplication artefact but the consequence of both consortia sizing to the same contracted ANS gas volume, and each states it in its own documents. CAVEAT recorded rather than a clean confirmation: the two rows share a corridor (both follow the Alaska Highway from a Prudhoe Bay GTP) and a capacity, so a future reviewer will ask this question again - the answer belongs in ResearcherNotes on both rows. Separately, P0146's LengthKnown=1700.00 is labelled 'km' while every source for that project says 1,700 MILES; that is a defect on P0146, flagged in cross_row_leads, not a reason to merge.

concerns.researcher_notes: IDENTITY / DUPLICATE ADJUDICATION - the headline question for this row. Conclusion: ASAP (P0293) is NOT a duplicate of Alaska LNG (P0147), and it has NOT been folded into AKLNG's Phase 1. It is also distinct from P0146 Alaska Pipeline Project and P0174 Denali. Evidence: (1) SPONSOR'S OWN WORDS - AGDC senior VP Frank Richards, quoted by Oil & Gas Journal and KTUU in June 2018: 'AGDC is advancing two [Alaska North Slope] gas pipeline projects on parallel paths but only one will be built'; the two 'share a common mainline alignment for more than 80% of the route' but AKLNG adds liquefaction and export. Mutual exclusivity plus a shared corridor is a redundancy relationship, not one project entered twice. (2) SEPARATE REGULATORY TRACKS - ASAP is permitted by the US Army Corps of Engineers under CWA s404 / RHA s10 (NOIs 2009 and 2014, Final SEIS 22 Jun 2018) and holds Alaska DNR right-of-way lease ADL 418997; AKLNG is a FERC project. Two dockets, two lead agencies, two sets of permits. (3) DIFFERENT PHYSICAL PROJECTS - ASAP: 737 mi, 36-inch mainline + 12-inch/29-30 mi Fairbanks lateral, 1,480 psig, 500 MMcf/d, in-state delivery into ENSTAR at Point MacKenzie. AKLNG's pipeline: 42-inch, ~3,500 MMcf/d, to a Nikiski liquefaction plant. Same corridor, different pipe. (4) STILL SEPARATE TODAY - AGDC's ASAP page (current): 'the corporation is primarily focused on the Alaska LNG Project. ASAP remains as the State's back up project'; AGDC's FY2026 Capital AFE (June 2025): ASAP 'was idled following the completion of major permitting and is not currently active', while Phase 1 FEED work proceeds under the AKLNG banner. ASAP was left dormant as the state's fallback, not absorbed. (5) Against P0146/P0174: those are the 2008-2012 Alaska Gasline Inducement Act-era EXPORT trunk proposals to Alberta by TransCanada/ExxonMobil and BP/ConocoPhillips respectively - different sponsors, different destinations, both cancelled; the P0146 shard already adjudicated those two as genuinely competing proposals rather than one project. No DUPLICATE flag is raised. The caveat is bookkeeping only: any Alaska North Slope capacity/length total that adds P0293 and P0147 together is double-counting a corridor that can only be built once.

The two differ in scope framing, receipt points, and capacity mechanics (Access Northeast bundled a large compressor buildout tied to New England utility RFPs; Project Maple is scoped around the Ramapo NY and Salem MA receipt points only). Given a search of Enbridge's own materials and independent press turned up no explicit linkage, the working finding is 'no evidence of a stated revival relationship' rather than a confident denial — flagged here and as a cross-row lead for whoever is sweeping P0144, since that row's own sources should be checked for any claim in the other direction.

concerns.recommendation: Keep both rows as recorded, no merge. P7450 (Kenai Beluga Pipeline / segment "Beluga Pipeline", Beluga -> Old Tyonek, 16.21 mi) and P7458 (Beluga Pipeline, Beluga -> Anchorage, 101.35 mi, 20-inch) are two real, physically and corporately distinct pipelines that happen to share the word "Beluga" and a common origin point at the Beluga area of west Cook Inlet. The name collision is a legitimate but confusing coincidence, not a data-entry duplicate, and is worth a permanent caveat note on both rows so a future researcher does not merge them on name alone.
concerns.researcher_notes: Three independent lines of evidence, none of them GEM's own wiki, all converge on the same negative verdict (not a duplicate): (1) CORPORATE/REGULATORY HISTORY -- the Regulatory Commission of Alaska's public notice of September 12, 2014 (Docket No. P-14-025, aws.state.ak.us id=174074, already the sheet's Owner ref) names 'Kenai Beluga Pipeline, LLC (KBPL), Beluga Pipeline Company (Beluga), Kenai Kachemak Pipeline, LLC (KKPL), Hilcorp Alaska, LLC d/b/a Cook Inlet Gas Gathering System (CIGGS), and Hilcorp Alaska, LLC d/b/a Kenai Nikiski Pipeline (KNPL)' as FIVE separate, pre-existing, separately-certificated applicants (holding CPCN Nos. 448, 711, 668 and 689 between them) jointly petitioning to fold their certificates into one, with KBPL surviving as the operating entity under amended CPCN 668. 'Beluga Pipeline Company' (Beluga) is listed as a distinct pre-2014 CPCN holder from KBPL itself -- proof the two 'Beluga' names were never one system administratively, only commonly owned (all five were already 100% Hilcorp Alaska, LLC subsidiaries by 2014). (2) ENVIRONMENTAL-REGULATORY DESCRIPTION -- the Alaska DEC AKG320000 'Statewide Oil and Gas Pipelines' general-permit fact sheet (dec.alaska.gov/media/mxmbp1n0/akg320000_fs_vfinal.pdf, already the sheet's Fuel ref) independently and explicitly describes two separate systems under two separate headings: 'the Beluga Pipeline section of Kenai Beluga Pipeline System' -- fed by the Tyonek Production Platform and KPL/Kaloa Junction gas, matching P7450 exactly -- versus, under its own separate heading two paragraphs later, the 'Beluga Natural Gas Transmission Pipeline' a.k.a. 'Beluga Power Plant Pipeline,' built 1984, 20-inch diameter, 'owned and operated by ENSTAR Natural Gas Company,' supplying 'the Beluga Power Plant to residential and commercial customers in Anchorage' -- matching P7458's sheet values (1984, 20-inch, Beluga-to-Anchorage) exactly, including a different owner/operator (ENSTAR/APC, not Hilcorp/Harvest/KBPL). (3) ROUTE GEOMETRY -- both PIDs' routes-repo GeoJSON traces (individual-routes/gas-pipelines/P7450.geojson, P7458.geojson) share an identical starting coordinate at Beluga but diverge into completely different corridors: P7450 runs southwest, haversine length ~16.2 mi, matching the sheet's 16.21 mi; P7458 runs east to Anchorage, haversine length ~101.2 mi, matching the sheet's 101.35 mi. This is internal corroboration only (not cited as a [ref] -- geometry is out of scope for the refs leg per the sweep SOP) but it independently reproduces the same split the two textual sources describe. PHMSA's March 2022 Final Order against Harvest Alaska, LLC (CPF No. 5-2021-023-NOPV) additionally confirms P7450's own pipeline is bi-directional, fed by 'West CIGGS sources' and the 'Beluga River Unit (BRU) Compressor,' passing through 'Kaloa Junction' -- entirely consistent with the Hilcorp/Harvest Cook Inlet gathering-and-transmission network described for P7450, and never mentions Anchorage or ENSTAR. Net: no evidence anywhere that these are the same pipe entered twice, and affirmative evidence from three independent origins (a state regulator's consolidation docket, a state environmental permit fact sheet, and route geometry) that they are not.

concerns.recommendation: No merge needed. Keep P7458 and P7450 as separate rows -- they are two distinct physical pipelines that happen to both carry the word 'Beluga'.
concerns.researcher_notes: ORCHESTRATOR-ASSIGNED ADJUDICATION: is P7458 (PipelineName 'Beluga Pipeline', blank SegmentName, 101.35 mi, 20-in, operating, row 3844) a duplicate of P7450 (PipelineName 'Kenai Beluga Pipeline', SegmentName 'Beluga Pipeline', 16.21 mi, no diameter, operating, row 3836)? VERDICT: NOT A DUPLICATE -- negative verdict, two distinct facilities. Evidence, four independent origins: (1) Alaska DEC APDES Pipeline GP Fact Sheet (dec.alaska.gov/media/mxmbp1n0/akg320000_fs_vfinal.pdf) has a dedicated subsection 'Beluga Natural Gas Transmission Pipeline' stating verbatim: 'The Beluga Power Plant Pipeline was built in 1984 and is owned and operated by ENSTAR Natural Gas Company. The Beluga Natural Gas Transmission Pipeline is a 20-inch diameter pipeline that supplies gas from the Beluga Power Plant to residential and commercial customers in Anchorage.' The SAME fact sheet, in its Hilcorp/Tyonek subsection, separately refers to 'the Beluga Pipeline section of Kenai Beluga Pipeline System' as the destination where Tyonek-area gas enters -- explicitly naming P7450's system as a DIFFERENT facility from ENSTAR's line. (2) Alaska DNR Donlin Gold special-area permit (dnr.alaska.gov/mlw/mining/large-mines/donlin/pdf/fh21-spo-044-sa.pdf) independently describes 'the existing ENSTAR 20-inch Beluga natural gas pipeline (BPL)' as the tie-in point for the proposed Donlin lateral -- again ENSTAR, 20-inch, matching P7458 exactly. (3) ConocoPhillips Alaska's Cook Inlet history timeline (conocophillipsalaska.com/ea/cookinlettimeline/) states twice, independently of DEC/DNR: 'In 1984, ENSTAR Natural Gas Company constructed a pipeline from Anchorage to the Beluga River Gas Field' -- confirms owner, year, and route for P7458 specifically. (4) The Regulatory Commission of Alaska's public notice for Docket P-14-025 (aws.state.ak.us/OnlinePublicNotices/Notices/View.aspx?id=174074, 2014) documents that 'Kenai Beluga Pipeline, LLC (KBPL), Beluga Pipeline Company (Beluga), Kenai Kachemak Pipeline, LLC (KKPL), Hilcorp Alaska, LLC d/b/a Cook Inlet Gas Gathering System (CIGGS), and Hilcorp Alaska, LLC d/b/a Kenai Nikiski Pipeline (KNPL)... are all owned 100 percent, directly or indirectly, by Hilcorp Alaska, LLC' and were consolidated into one CPCN (No. 668) under KBPL -- i.e., the corporate entity actually named 'Beluga Pipeline Company' is a wholly Hilcorp-owned entity, structurally and historically unrelated to ENSTAR. (5) PHMSA Final Order CPF No. 5-2021-023-NOPV (2022-03-28, against Harvest Alaska LLC) separately discusses a bi-directional 'Beluga Transmission Pipeline' at Kaloa Junction tied to the Beluga River Unit (BRU) and 'West CIGGS' sources -- consistent with the Hilcorp/Harvest-side KBPL 'Beluga Pipeline' segment (P7450), not ENSTAR's line. CONCLUSION: P7458 = ENSTAR's own 'Beluga Natural Gas Transmission Pipeline' / 'Beluga Power Plant Pipeline' (Beluga Power Plant -> Anchorage, 20-in, built 1984, 100% ENSTAR-owned). P7450 = the former 'Beluga Pipeline Company' segment of the Hilcorp-owned, consolidated Kenai Beluga Pipeline System (KBPL, near Kaloa Junction on the west side of Cook Inlet), unrelated in ownership, history, or route to P7458. Both rows should stand as-is; no merge, no relabel. LENGTH PLAUSIBILITY (also orchestrator-flagged): 101.35 mi is plausible despite the Beluga field sitting only ~40 mi west of Anchorage across the inlet, because ENSTAR's route does not cross the inlet directly -- it runs north and east around the head of Cook Inlet along the coast. Internal (uncitable, GOIT-GGIT-pipeline-routes repo) geometry check on P7458.geojson (127-point MultiLineString) sums to ~101.24 mi via haversine, closely matching the recorded 101.35 mi and confirming the routing explanation; this is our own measurement, not a citable second source, and is not staged as a proposed_ref for the Length unit (see fills[] Length record, which remains UNRESOLVED for an independent PUBLISHED mileage figure).

What I actually verified: (1) Utility Dive (real content fetched and read directly, not just the search snippet -- the default url_verifier UA gets a 403 bot-wall on this host, but a browser UA gets 200 with the full article; same false-negative class the script's docstring already documents for other bot-walled hosts) states the CP18-37 compressor project raises Sierrita from 200,846 Dth/d to 'almost 323,000 Dth/d' (~323 MMcf/d total, i.e. a ~122,000 Dth/d increment), cost ~$56 million -- the SAME $56M figure gem.wiki attributes to 'Sierrita Pima Expansion' (P2615). (2) Kinder Morgan's own SEC Form 8-K earnings exhibit for Q4 2019 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1506307/000150630720000002/kmi2019q48-kex991.htm, verified) describes a Sierrita expansion 'increas[ing] the pipeline's capacity by approximately 323,000 Dth/d to 524,000 Dth/d,' completion expected Q2 2020. (3) EIA's Today in Energy piece ({EIA}, verified) independently confirms a '0.32 Bcf/d Sierrita Pima Expansion... completed in early 2020' -- 0.32 Bcf/d = 320 MMcf/d, matching P2615's recorded Capacity almost exactly, and NOT naming any separate 'Puerto Libertad Expansion.' (4) Kinder Morgan's own FY2022 10-K ({KMI2022}, verified, page/line: 'Sierrita 35% 60 [miles] 0.52 [Bcf/d capacity]') reports Sierrita's TOTAL system capacity as of FY2022 as 0.52 Bcf/d = 520 MMcf/d -- i.e. 200 (original, confirmed via the 2018 10-K's '60 [miles] 0.20 [Bcf/d]' entry for the same asset) + 320 (Pima Expansion), with NO further increment for a separate 427 MMcf/d 'Puerto Libertad Expansion.' If a second, independent 427 MMcf/d project had actually gone into service, KMI's own reported system capacity would be far higher than 520. (5) A Mexican federal government document (SENER/CRE status report, Oct 2017, https://www.gob.mx/cms/uploads/attachment/file/265260/Estatus_Gasoductos_octubre_2017.pdf, verified) lists the ORIGINAL Sierrita line (Tucson-Sasabe, 97 km, in service Dec 2014, Sierrita Gas LLC = MGI-Mitsui-KM) at 195 mmpcd capacity with a footnote that it 'sera expandida hasta 770 mmpcd' (will be expanded up to 770 mmpcd) per CFE's requirements -- a THIRD, still different, larger PLANNED ceiling figure from Oct 2017, distinct from both 627 and the 520/524 actually realized. This confirms 'Puerto Libertad' is the name of the Sonora town where a SEPARATE, IENova/CFE-owned Mexican pipeline (Sasabe-Pto. Libertad, 'Proyecto Noroeste' Tramo I, 218 km, also in service Dec 2014) receives Sierrita's exported gas -- i.e. 'Puerto Libertad' names the downstream Mexican market/destination the US compressor expansion was built to serve, not a second, separate US-side pipeline construction project. I could NOT independently verify the '627 MMcf/d' / '427 MMcf/d increment' figures against any primary document -- the only place they surfaced was gem.wiki's own narrative and one search-tool synthesized answer that also claimed the FederalRegister.gov notice states these numbers; when I fetched that exact URL directly, it returned FederalRegister.gov's bot-wall CAPTCHA page (title-tag text only, no article body), so that synthesis could not have come from the real page and should not be trusted -- flagging this as a near-miss so nobody downstream treats it as read. Net: P2614 and P2615 both describe -- with high confidence -- the SAME physical CP18-37 compressor project (same new compressor station in Pima County AZ, same $56M cost figure, same Oct 2018 FERC approval window, same 2020 completion), but carry two different, non-additive capacity figures (427 vs 320) neither of which, if simply added to each other or to the original 200, matches KMI's own verified FY2022 total of 520 MMcf/d. This is either a duplicate row or, at minimum, a spec error on Capacity -- not a fillable REFS_ADDED. I have NOT staged a confirming ref for Capacity on this row; see the paired fills[] entry (UNRESOLVED).

concerns.researcher_notes: PipelineType is currently blank on the sheet (not in this batch's worklist scope, so no fills[] object staged for it, but it is a real gap worth flagging under the classification check). Not calling this existence or duplicate doubt -- the physical pipe is real and this is the right row for it -- but the tracker currently carries it with no PipelineType at all, and the evidence points to 'gathering' rather than leaving it to default to a transmission-style read.

concerns.recommendation: reclassify PipelineType from 'gathering' to 'transmission'
concerns.researcher_notes: GEM's current PipelineType = 'gathering'. Every independent source that classifies this line at all calls it a TRANSMISSION pipeline, not a gathering line: Wikipedia states outright 'The Garden Banks Pipeline is a 30-inch diameter natural gas transmission pipeline'; Enbridge's own 2020 factsheet section header 'Garden Banks Pipeline' states 'The Garden Banks Pipeline is a 30-inch-diameter, Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC)-regulated offshore natural gas transmission pipeline' and lists 'Nature of asset: Offshore natural gas transmission pipeline'; the Oct 2024 Enbridge press release calls it 'Enbridge's downstream FERC-regulated Garden Banks Gas Pipeline'. The 2008 Enbridge offshore-gt.com corridor table is itself the clearest internal evidence of the distinction GEM's vocab is trying to capture: within the same 'Garden Banks Corridor' it lists 'Garden Banks Pipeline' (50 mi, 1000 MMcf/d, Regulating Agency = FERC, i.e. transmission-grade jurisdictional pipeline) as a SEPARATE line item from 'Magnolia Gathering Lateral' (50 mi, 250 MMcf/d, Regulating Agency = MMS, i.e. the actual gathering asset in the same corridor). So Enbridge's own operational taxonomy treats Garden Banks Pipeline itself as the FERC-jurisdictional transmission line and reserves 'gathering' for the separate Magnolia lateral. GEM's controlled vocab (docs/reference/controlled_vocab.md) allows both 'transmission' and 'gathering' as PipelineType values, so this is a real classification error to fix, not a vocab gap.

concerns.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE AND CLASSIFICATION: the underlying pipe is real, FERC-certificated, gas transmission infrastructure -- not in question. What is wrong is treating it as cancelled. GEM's own dates (ShelvedYear=2010, CancelledYear=2012) line up almost exactly with real FERC milestones for TEAM 2012 (PF10-21 pre-filing NOI published 2010-08-26, 75 FR 52524; formal application 2011-02-11, FERC Docket CP11-67-000; amended 2011-06-30; EA notice 2011-09-02, 36-inch pipe through Greene/Fayette/Franklin/Adams/Fulton Counties PA plus a Bedford Compressor Station upgrade in Bedford County PA) -- but instead of ending in cancellation, a FERC 'Combined Notice of Filings' dated 2012-09-12 (77 FR, Docket CP11-67) records Texas Eastern's own 'TEAM 2012 In-Service Filing -- CP11-67 Compliance to be effective 11/1/2012.' The EIA Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook (eia.gov/naturalgas/pipelines/EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjectsAug2026.xlsx, sheet 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)', row 731) independently corroborates this from a completely different agency/dataset: 'TETCO TEAM 2012 Expansion' / Texas Eastern Transmission / Status=Completed / Completed Date 2012-10-31 / Docket CP11-67. Two independent government sources (FERC's own docket record and EIA's separately-compiled tracking dataset) agree this project reached commercial service, not cancellation, in late 2012 -- squarely on top of GEM's recorded CancelledYear. Texas Eastern did not stop there: a second FERC pre-filing (PF12-19, NOI 2012-10-15, 77 FR 62507) opened for the 'Texas Eastern and Appalachia Market Expansion Project 2014 (TEAM 2014)' -- construction/modification in PA/WV/OH/KY/TN/AL/MS -- which became Docket CP13-84 (application 2013-03-21; EA notice 2013-09-23) and, per EIA workbook row 785, also reached 'Completed' status with an in-service date of 2014-11-07. This is a textbook case of the pattern this sweep was told to test for: a project shelved/re-scoped under FERC review is not cancelled if it is later built under the docket's actual project name. GEM's row 'TEMAX Pipeline Expansion' appears to be an informal/garbled label for this TEAM program rather than a name FERC or any source actually used (searched: no FERC docket, EIA row, or press hit for the literal string 'TEMAX'). DUPLICATE CHECK: neither 'TEAM 2012'/CP11-67 nor 'TEAM 2014'/CP13-84 appears as a named pipeline/segment in the 45-row US-gas cohort roster provided for this batch, so I cannot confirm from the material given to me whether either successor is ALREADY tracked as a separate GEM PID elsewhere in the full 131-column Gas tab (outside this batch's scope). concerns.recommendation: reclassify PipelineType from 'transmission' to 'gathering' -- FERC's own jurisdictional ruling on this exact system
concerns.researcher_notes: The sheet's current PipelineType='transmission' is supported only by a citation to eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php#pipelines, a navigation page that does not name this pipeline (builder's own relevance check: name_found=false) -- so the value was effectively uncited, not merely under-cited. Independent, on-point evidence says the opposite: on 2024-09-27 FERC issued an Order on Petition for Order to Show Cause (Energy Transfer LP's petition, docket proceedings around CP24-122) applying the 'primary function test' and finding the LEG System -- despite its large 30-42in diameter and high operating pressure, both typical of transmission -- is legally and functionally a GATHERING system: a spine-like configuration gathering unprocessed gas from ~775 wellhead receipt points along its length, with no FERC NGA jurisdiction. Reported independently by a law firm (Van Ness Feldman, via natlawreview.com) and by trade press (naturalgasintel.com, 'Williams Prevails as FERC Rules Louisiana LEG System a Natural Gas Gathering Pipe'), both describing the same primary document with matching specifics (174 mi, 1.8 Bcf/d, 775 receipt points). Williams' own SEC 10-Qs likewise describe LEG only as 'natural gas gathering assets' / 'gathering system', never as an interstate transmission line. `gathering` is a valid value in the repo's controlled vocabulary (docs/reference/controlled_vocab.md). This is a genuine misclassification, not a close call -- FERC's order is a formal jurisdictional determination on this exact system.

concerns.researcher_notes: The pipeline itself is REAL and its data is correct, but it is very likely mis-parented under the wrong pipeline family. GEM's own wiki article bundles two things that both operator disclosures and the US government's independent dataset treat as SEPARATE NGPL projects: (1) the 'Gulf Coast Southbound'/'Gulf Coast Expansion Project' (GCEP) Phases I-III, an interstate reversal corridor running Chicago, IL -> Agua Dulce Hub/Corpus Christi/Sabine Pass, TX and Henry, LA, built to move Midcontinent/Marcellus/Utica gas SOUTH for LNG export feed, and (2) the 'Lockridge Extension Pipeline' (a.k.a. 'Lockridge to Waha Project'), an entirely-intrastate-Texas project that instead brings Permian-area gas INTO the Waha Hub via 'an extension of its Amarillo system' -- geographically and functionally distinct, with no state-border crossing (EIA: Beg_State TX, End_State TX, Pipeline Type 'Intrastate', vs GCEP's IL->TX interstate reversal). Evidence: (a) Kinder Morgan's own Q3-2020 earnings release (BOE Report, verified live) lists them as two separate line items in the same paragraph -- 'Construction is progressing on NGPL's Gulf Coast Southbound project. The approximately $203 million project ... will increase southbound capacity ... to serve Cheniere's Corpus Christi Liquefaction facility ... Construction is complete on NGPL's approximately $51 million Lockridge to Waha Project ... The project enables NGPL to deliver up to 500,000 Dth/d to the Waha Hub with an extension of its Amarillo system' -- two different projects, two different cost figures, two different purposes, described back-to-back as distinct. (b) EIA's 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects' database (U.S. government, independent of GEM and of Kinder Morgan) carries them as three separate line items across two different sheets: 'NGPL Gulf Coast Southbound Project (Phase II)' and '(Phase III)' (interstate reversal, IL->TX, $145M each, in the current 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects' sheet) versus 'Lockridge Extension Pipeline' (intrastate, TX->TX, $51.6M, 16.84 mi, 30in, 500 MMcf/d, completed 2020-09-28, docket CP19-52, note: 'Bring additional Permian production to Waha hub') in the 'Historical Projects (1996-2020)' sheet. (c) NGPL's own dedicated open-season notice for 'Gulf Coast Expansion Project Phase 3' (pipeline2.kindermorgan.com PDF, one of this row's harvested wiki citations, opened and read in full via pdftotext) describes GCEP Phases 1-3 exclusively as the Illinois/Iowa-to-Gulf-Coast southbound corridor and never mentions Lockridge or Waha at all -- if Lockridge were truly a phase of Gulf Coast Southbound, NGPL's own project-family solicitation document would be the place to expect it, and it is absent. Net: the ProjectID is not a phantom, not a duplicate of another Texas row on the roster (no close match on name/route/specs among the other 44 rows), and not commodity-misclassified (it is unambiguously a natural gas pipeline) -- but filing it as a 'segment' of 'Gulf Coast Southbound Pipeline' overstates a physical/administrative link that the cited sources do not support. Harvested-citation coverage for this row: 7 citations on the wiki page; I opened/read 4 in full (EIA data.php landing page + the EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjects_Jan2021.xlsx it points to, BOE Report, the GCEP Phase 3 open-season PDF) and could NOT read 3 -- rbnenergy.com/node/11661 (HTTP 403, and its Wayback snapshot 429'd from web.archive.org's rate limiter on repeated tries), seekingalpha.com (HTTP 403, paywalled/bot-walled), and the Federal Register CP20-14-000 notice for the '134th Street Lateral Project' (opened and read in full, but it is correctly cited on the wiki page for a DIFFERENT section/segment of the same page -- an Illinois/Indiana lateral, not Lockridge -- so it is irrelevant to this segment rather than unread evidence). concerns.recommendation: change Status from 'operating' to 'retired' (as a gas pipeline) -- Trailblazer has been formally abandoned by FERC and physically repurposed to transport CO2, not natural gas; this is exactly the batch brief's flagged lead for P0266

DUPLICATE: checked against the full 46-row roster (P0151...P3601) -- no separate 'Trailblazer CO2' or similarly-named row exists, so this is not a redundancy question, only a status/classification one on this same row. CLASSIFICATION/STATUS (the batch brief's central lead): Tallgrass announced in 2022 that it would convert Trailblazer from natural gas to CO2 transport service. S&P Global (2022-06-01, via Wayback) reported Trailblazer Pipeline Company LLC and Rockies Express Pipeline LLC filed for FERC authorization (Docket CP22-468, filed 2022-05-27) to abandon ~392 miles of the Trailblazer gas system in place and repurpose it for CO2, while gas shippers were to be rerouted onto new REX leased capacity/laterals. FERC's own Federal Register notice (2023-04-06) confirms an Environmental Assessment was issued for 'Trailblazer Pipeline Company LLC, Rockies Express Pipeline LLC' covering this conversion. A second Federal Register notice (2024-10-09) confirms FERC's October 23, 2023 Order 'Issuing Certificate and Granting Abandonment' authorized the project (the 'Trailblazer Conversion Project' in Weld County, CO and Kimball County, NE), that construction began January 4, 2024, and that Trailblazer/REX requested (and were later granted, per the docket) an extension to complete the Hereford Ranch and Redtail Compressor Stations by December 23, 2024. Oil & Gas Journal (2024-05-06, via Wayback since the live OGJ URL serves randomized unrelated article content to non-browser fetches) reported Trailblazer/REX holding a CO2 transport open season under the FERC-approved conversion, confirming the project moved from authorization into commercialization. ADM's own investor-facing overview PDF states the timeline plainly: '2022 Announce Project ... 2024 Begin CO2 Service' and that the project 'converts the nearly 400-mile Trailblazer pipeline from natural gas service to carbon dioxide (CO2)... to permanently store more than 10 million metric tons of CO2 annually.' Nebraska Examiner (2025-09-24 and 2025-10-10) both independently confirm commercial CO2 shipments began October 3, 2025, moving CO2 from 11 Nebraska/Colorado/Wyoming ethanol plants ~392 miles to Wyoming for sequestration, explicitly stating 'the Trailblazer pipeline formerly carried natural gas' and 'much of the pipeline was already built as the natural gas line.' Pipeline & Gas Journal (2025-09, verified separately) restates the same 392-mile CO2-transport-begins story. Six independent origins (FERC/Federal Register x2, S&P Global, OGJ, ADM, Nebraska Examiner/PGJ) converge: Trailblazer is no longer in gas service. Per docs/reference/controlled_vocab.md, 'retired' is the correct Status value for a formally abandoned/decommissioned gas asset -- there is no 'converted' or repurposed-commodity value in the Status vocab, and this GGIT (gas) tracker is not the place to add a new CO2 row for the same pipe; that is a separate tracking-scope question for Baird, not resolved here. GEM's LastUpdated=2023-08-30 predates the October 2023 abandonment order and the 2024-2025 physical conversion/start of CO2 service, which is why the sheet is now stale rather than simply wrong-when-entered. concerns.recommendation: verify whether StartLocation/EndLocation should be swapped (Mississippi Canyon Block 920 as Start, West Delta Block 68 as End) to match actual gas-flow direction and this roster's own Start=upstream-field/End=downstream-delivery convention; separately, correct FuelSource off 'West Delta Block 68' to the actual upstream source (Independence Hub / Mississippi Canyon Block 920 fields)
concerns.researcher_notes: Four independent sources describing the pipeline's function all agree on ONE gas-flow direction: Mississippi Canyon Block 920 (the Independence Hub central processing platform, the upstream source) toward West Delta Block 68 (a shallow-water manifold platform where the gas interconnects with — and is delivered into — Tennessee Gas Pipeline for onward transport to onshore markets). Anadarko/BusinessWire: 'connects the Hub platform to onshore markets via an interconnect with the Tennessee Gas Pipeline at Enterprise's West Delta block 68 shallow-water manifold platform.' OGJ (Jan 2006): pipeline 'will transport the gas to the Tennessee Gas Pipeline system in West Delta Block 68.' OGJ (Nov 2006 special report): 'connects the Independence Hub [platform] to an interconnect with Tennessee Gas Pipeline in West Delta Block 68.' Allseas (contractor, own history page): 'the pipeline transports gas from the Independence Hub Facility in Mississippi Canyon 920 to the West Delta 68 platform.' The sheet's current Location [ref] unit has StartLocation='West Delta Block 68' and EndLocation='Mississippi Canyon Block 920' — i.e. the REVERSE of the direction every independent source describes. The one source that reads consistently with the sheet's current direction is the sheet's own cited primary lead, niobium.tech (Jahde et al. 2007, written by the pipeline's own design engineers): 'ITP initiates from West Delta Block 68... and terminates at Mississippi Canyon Block 920' — but read in context this sentence is in the 'Pipeline Route Selection' section describing how the pipe-LAY vessel worked (shallow water to deep water), not the direction gas flows once in service; Allseas' own account of the SAME lay operation (Solitaire delivering the project in 2006) states the finished pipeline moves gas the opposite way. This roster's other offshore-to-onshore rows (P0223 Nautilus: 'Ship Shoal Block 207, Green Canyon Corridor -> Louisiana'; P0217 Mississippi Canyon Gas Pipeline: 'Mississippi Canyon -> Louisiana') consistently put the upstream field as Start and the downstream delivery point as End, so a swap here would also align this row with the roster's own convention. This is not a phantom-pipeline or duplicate concern — the place names in the Location cell are both correct and independently verified, it is only the Start/End assignment (and the copy of that assignment into FuelSource) that is doubtful. FuelSource is separately wrong on the same logic: the GEM schema gotcha for gas-sheet FuelSource is 'the upstream gas source feeding the line — a field, plant, or facility,' not a downstream delivery point, so 'West Delta Block 68' (the TGP interconnect/exit point) is very likely backwards for this column too; the correct value is the Independence Hub platform / the Atwater Valley-DeSoto Canyon-Lloyd Ridge-Mississippi Canyon field complex it gathers (OGJ special report names the ten anchor fields feeding the Hub). Left as a validity flag rather than an auto-fix per the 'never auto-apply a reference value' rule and because the StartState/Province='Gulf of Mexico' / EndState/Province='Gulf of Mexico' pair is genuinely defensible as written — this pipeline is subsea/offshore end-to-end between two OCS platforms and never itself makes onshore landfall in any state (delivery to shore happens downstream, inside Tennessee Gas Pipeline), so no state-name correction is proposed for either State/Province cell; this differs from the scope note's other flagged rows (Garden Banks, etc.) where a real state IS available.

concerns.researcher_notes:
Project-history reconstruction from primary press sources: (1) VNG's original, larger proposal was the 'Header Improvement Project' (HIP) -- three new pipelines totaling 24 miles (Transco Interconnect Pipeline 6.2 mi + Quantico Parallel Pipeline 3.3 mi + Mechanicsville Parallel Pipeline 14.6 mi, all 30-inch diameter), spanning Prince William, Fauquier, Hanover, New Kent, and Charles City counties plus the City of Chesapeake, meant to supply the C4GT and Chickahominy gas power plants, at a cost the Bay Journal states explicitly as '$346 million' (bayjournal.com, 'Virginia board rejects application for natural gas pipeline expansion project'). The Virginia SCC REJECTED HIP on Dec. 1, 2020 (same Bay Journal article: 'the Dec. 1 decision to dismiss a request for a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity... the Header Improvement Project'; VNG's own spokesperson is quoted saying the company was 'preparing' a new, separate filing). (2) That new filing -- reported by Virginia Mercury on 2020-12-16 as filed 'earlier this week' -- is a SMALLER, SCALED-DOWN project (the 'Interconnect Project' / GEM's 'VNG Interconnect'): 'The new project, estimated to cost $205 million, would add almost 10 miles of pipeline and an additional compressor station in Prince William County.' EIA's Aug 2026 release (sheet 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)', Excel row 1143) independently states the identical figures for 'VNG Interconnect': 10 miles, $205 million, 245 MMcf/d, Cancelled. (3) The withdrawal notice for this SAME smaller project (Chesapeake Climate Action Network, 2021-03-23) states outright that 'VNG had planned to build the Interconnect in Northern Virginia primarily based off of plans from a previously cancelled project called the Header Improvement Project (HIP)' -- i.e. the Interconnect Project deliberately REUSED part of HIP's design (most likely the Transco Interconnect Pipeline 6.2 mi + Quantico Parallel Pipeline 3.3 mi = 9.5 mi, which rounds to Virginia Mercury's 'almost 10 miles' and EIA's 10 mi), while DROPPING the Mechanicsville Parallel Pipeline (14.6 mi) and the C4GT-specific scope. GEM's P5990 row is named/dated after the SMALLER project (title 'VNG Interconnect', CancelledYear 2021, matching the 2021-03-23 withdrawal) but its Length (24.00 mi) and SegmentCost ($346,000,000) values were sourced from documents describing the LARGER, EARLIER, REJECTED project (HIP) -- a genuine conflation of two sequential, differently-scoped filings that happen to share overlapping route segments and the same corporate sponsor. Diameter (30 in) is NOT flagged as an error: it is a per-segment physical spec (pipe diameter of the specific Transco Interconnect + Quantico Parallel segments), not a project-total aggregate, so it plausibly carries over unchanged between the two filings since the same physical pipe design was reused -- unlike Length and Cost, which are project-total sums that necessarily shrink when the Mechanicsville segment and C4GT-specific facilities are dropped.

ORCHESTRATOR ADJUDICATION 2026-09-14 — this SUPERSEDES the 'CONFIRMED DUPLICATE' verdict this shard reached and the retire-P3200 recommendation in its cross_row_leads. The row agent's PROJECT HISTORY was right and is adopted in full; only the direction of the fix is reversed.
P3200 and P5990 are NOT the same project. They are two successive Virginia Natural Gas applications to the Virginia SCC:
  (a) HEADER IMPROVEMENT PROJECT (HIP) — three new 30-inch pipelines totalling ~24 mi (Transco Interconnect Pipeline 6.2 mi + Quantico Parallel Pipe 3.3 mi + Mechanicsville Parallel Pipe 14.6 mi = 24.1 mi), ~$346M, across Prince William, Fauquier, Hanover, New Kent and Charles City counties, sized for the proposed C4GT plant in Charles City County. DISMISSED by the SCC in December 2020 once C4GT's conditions could not be met.
  (b) VNG INTERCONNECT — the renamed, downsized successor filed 2020-12-14: ~10 mi (about 6 mi Prince William + 4 mi Fauquier, i.e. HIP's two northern segments with the 14.6 mi Mechanicsville leg dropped), 245 MMcf/d, $205M, plus a compressor station near Nokesville and Hanover metering upgrades. WITHDRAWN March 2021. This is EIA's single 'VNG Interconnect' row (Aug 2026, sheet 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)', Excel row 1143).
THIS ROW (P5990) HOLDS HIP'S DATA, NOT THE INTERCONNECT'S: 24 mi, 30 in, $346M, Prince William to Fauquier — and BOTH of its live-sheet refs are Header-Improvement-Project pages (Chesapeake Climate's 'Header Injustice Project' page; the Bay Journal's report of the SCC's Dec 1 2020 dismissal). P3200 holds the Interconnect's data (10 mi, 245 MMcf/d, $205M) and matches EIA.
THEREFORE THE DEFECT ON THIS ROW IS ITS NAME, NOT ITS NUMBERS. The row agent proposed the opposite — rewriting LengthKnown down to ~10 mi and SegmentCost down to $205M to match the name. That is rejected: it would make P5990 a second copy of P3200 and delete the Header Improvement Project — a real, separately-filed, separately-dismissed project — from the database entirely, while overwriting correctly-sourced values with another project's figures. Pembina acquired Veresen in 2017 (Reuters, 2017-05-01, via Wayback -- confirms the $7.1B Pembina-Veresen deal and Veresen's Jordan Cove project, but this article and the Bloomberg 2017-09-22 refiling article both discuss only Jordan Cove/Veresen-Pembina, never naming 'Pacific Connector,' so neither is cited as a pipeline-specific ref per the relevance rule). No source found states Williams' original 49.5%+ interest was ever divested to Pembina/Veresen, nor that Pembina holds 100% of Pacific Connector specifically. concerns.recommendation: Correct EndState/Province and EndCountryOrArea to Minnesota / United States; the pipeline as proposed does not physically cross into Canada.
concerns.researcher_notes: GEM records EndState/Province=Manitoba, EndCountryOrArea=Canada, EndPrefecture/District=Emerson-Franklin -- i.e. treats this as a US-Canada border-crossing line. Three independent, dated sources all place the physical terminus in northwestern Minnesota, US, not Canada: (1) WBI Energy's own spokesperson Laura Lueder, quoted on the record in the Pierce County Tribune (2020-02-21): 'Our proposal is to go from the Tioga area to northwestern Minnesota, which is near the Emerson natural gas hub. Our other large gas pipelines connect at that hub and then the gas moves from there to larger markets, such as Chicago.' -- i.e. WBI's own pipe ends in Minnesota near (not at/in) the Emerson hub; (2) EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook records State(s)=ND,MN, Beg_State=ND, End_State=MN, and Crosses State Border=Yes (a US interstate designation, not an international one) in every release 2020-03 through 2026-08; (3) offshore-technology.com's project profile states the pipeline 'will start in North Dakota (the US) and ends in Minnesota (the US).' A Federal Register full-text search for '"Tioga to Emerson"' returns zero documents (checked 2026-09-15 via the FederalRegister.gov API), consistent with no DOE/FECM Presidential Permit or FERC Section 3 export/import authorization ever having been sought for this project -- expected if it never crosses the international border. A Canada Energy Regulator site search for the same terms returned no usable results (client-rendered search page, inconclusive either way -- not relied on). The routes-repo geojson's easternmost vertex sits at (-97.208086, 49.005584), about 0.6 km north of the 49th parallel -- fractionally inside Manitoba -- which reads as an artifact of digitizing to the Emerson hub landmark itself rather than evidence the pipe crosses the border; 'Emerson' in the project's own name is the name of the interconnect hub it was designed to reach, not proof its pipe enters Canada. Recommend GEM's end-location cells be corrected to Minnesota/United States (EndPrefecture/District cleared, since 'Emerson-Franklin' is a Manitoba municipality that would no longer apply); no route-geometry replacement is proposed, only the attribute correction. Commodity classification is NOT in question: WBI's own spokesperson calls it 'a large interstate natural gas pipeline system,' EIA classifies it in the Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook, and offshore-technology.com calls it 'the onshore gas pipeline' -- this is correctly tracked as gas, not NGL/crude, despite sitting in Bakken oil country.

NOTE TO DISPATCH BRIEF: the row was flagged as intrastate with FERC records expected thin/absent -- that expectation does NOT hold for this specific segment: Carlsbad Gateway holds an interstate NGA blanket certificate (Docket CP18-538-000) and filed this prior-notice request under it, so a full FERC/Federal Register record exists and is the strongest available source for this row. ROUTE CHECK: the routes-repo geojson for P7109 is internally labeled RouteName='Lea County Expansion', LineName='Carlsbad Gateway Pipeline' (not 'Agua Blanca'/'Targa Red Hills Interconnect') -- initially looked like a possible route/sheet mismatch. Checked Targa Resources' 10-Q (trgp-10q_20180630.htm) and MPLX's most recent 10-K Exhibit 21.1 subsidiary list for 'Carlsbad' -- zero hits in either, ruling OUT Carlsbad Gateway as a named Targa or MPLX subsidiary and as part of the 4-way Agua Blanca Joint Venture (WhiteWater/WPX-Devon/MPLX/Targa) that owns the mainline system. concerns.recommendation: verify true system terminus — the pipeline reportedly loops back into Minnesota, terminating at International Falls, MN, USA, not at Fort Frances, ON, Canada
concerns.researcher_notes: Both the operator's own about-us page (via Wayback capture 2025-05-03) and the CER-hosted company fact sheet describe the pipeline's route as: 'takes gas from the TC Energy pipeline at Spruce Siding, Manitoba south of Lake of the Woods through Minnesota into Ontario and back into Minnesota at International Falls' / '...travels south of Lake of the Woods, through northeastern Minnesota, into Ontario and back into Minnesota, terminating at International Falls.' Both sources are explicit that the single 270 km asset crosses the US-Canada border three times (Manitoba->Minnesota->Ontario->Minnesota) and that its far terminus is International Falls, MN, USA — not Fort Frances, ON, which is only the point where the line re-enters Ontario partway along the route (also named as a served Ontario community in the home page and fact sheet, alongside Rainy River, Stratton, Barwick, Emo, Devlin). The digitized route (../GOIT-GGIT-pipeline-routes/data/individual-routes/gas-pipelines/P7125.geojson, 1 feature, 89 points) also stops at Fort Frances (-93.42234,48.61399) and does not extend to International Falls — so the geometry is a partial trace of the same asset, consistent with the sheet's shorter, plausibly-incomplete endpoint. This is single-origin (both text sources trace to the same company/EFG family; a second, independent source stating 'International Falls' specifically as the far terminus was searched for — FERC eLibrary docket text, NEB/CER historical orders, press — but not found before the session's web-search budget was exhausted), so I am flagging rather than correcting outright: recommend verifying against CPMI's FERC tariff (which would state the certificated end point) or a CER facilities application before changing EndLocation/EndState/EndCountryOrArea. If confirmed, the route geojson is also a candidate for extension under §8 (not fabricated here).

The FERC EIS explicitly places the true receipt points/origin at the Cheyenne Hub in Weld County, Colorado (interconnects with Colorado Interstate Gas Co. and Wyoming Interstate Co.), and the true delivery points/terminus in Kiowa County, Kansas (interconnects with Southern Star Central, ANR Pipeline, Northern Natural Gas, Panhandle Eastern Pipe Line, and Kansas Gas Service), plus secondary delivery points in Scott and Ford counties. Kinder Morgan's own current operations page independently states the same shape: the system 'extends from near the Wyoming-Colorado border to South Central Kansas.' Trade press (industrialinfo.com) independently names the specific towns: 'originating in the Cheyenne Hub area of northern Colorado, near Greeley, and terminating near Greensburg, Kansas' -- Greensburg is the Kiowa County seat, consistent with the FERC EIS's Kiowa County delivery points. Three independent sources (FERC primary + KM operator page + industrialinfo trade press) agree the current Start/End fields are mid-route counties, not the actual termini. Candidate values given above use the town/hub names the sources actually name; a researcher should pick the exact facility-level point GEM's schema wants (Cheyenne Hub vs. a specific town name near it).

CONTESTED (Status / EndState/Province / Location): GEM records Status=operating with EndState/Province=California and EndLocation implying the pipeline still reaches California. It does not. The historic ~700-mile Southern Trails system (converted ARCO Four Corners Line 90, crude-to-gas, Docket CP99-163-000) had two California-touching pieces: a never-activated West Zone (Essex, CA to Long Beach, CA, ~209 mi, certificate later vacated/abandoned by FERC, c. 2004-05) and a California sliver of the East Zone. FERC authorized abandonment-in-place of the East Zone's California-to-Arizona segments (~220 mi) in Docket CP17-__ / the 2018 NOI and 2020 extension order; Phase 1 abandonment completed June 29, 2019 per the operator's compliance filings referenced in the extension notice. Only the ~268-mile New Mexico/Arizona/Utah remainder (sold/transferred to the Navajo Tribal Utility Authority, serving Red Mesa, Kayenta, and Tuba City) is operating today. Per the batch instruction to 'distinguish the eastern segment operates from the pipeline operates': the EASTERN (NM/AZ/UT) segment operates; the pipeline as GEM currently attributes it (reaching California) does not. Status=operating is defensible ONLY if read as 'the surviving NM/AZ/UT segment is operating' -- the California endpoint and any capacity/length figure implying a live California connection is stale.

Roster check: no other PID in the 46-row US-West roster corresponds to Southern Trails or any segment/alias of it -- not a duplicate. Existence confirmed beyond doubt (multiple FERC dockets, an active operator website capture, and continuing trade coverage through at least 2020). Classification (gas pipeline) confirmed. This is one of three rows the batch brief flagged as having a plausible status issue; recommend adding a ResearcherNotes flag on Status (not changing Status itself, since the surviving segment genuinely operates) plus correcting EndState/Province and EndLocation off California to Arizona/Utah (the pipeline's current terminus serving Kayenta/Tuba City, AZ) -- see the paired Location finding below.

CONTESTED (Owner1 / Owner1%): GEM records Owner1 = 'Southern Trails Pipeline Co' at 100%. This is the pre-2016 corporate name and is stale as a complete answer, but the successor picture is genuinely split rather than a single clean substitution: (1) Questar Corporation (parent of Southern Trails Pipeline Co) was acquired by Dominion Energy in 2016; Dominion's Questar Pipeline business (including Southern Trails) was then sold to Southwest Gas Holdings, closing Dec 31, 2021, and the surviving interstate-pipeline entities were rebranded 'MountainWest' effective April 1, 2022 -- a verified press release explicitly names a renamed subsidiary 'MountainWest Southern Trails Pipeline Company.' (2) Separately and earlier, Dominion Energy negotiated to transfer/sell the operating (NM/AZ/UT) segment to the Navajo Tribal Utility Authority (NTUA) starting with a signing ceremony Nov 28, 2017, subject to FERC approval expected in 2018 -- consistent with the 2018 FERC NOI and the 2019-2020 abandonment/extension dockets for the California/Arizona legs. I could not fully reconcile, from public sources in the time available, whether NTUA now owns the surviving pipe outright (with 'MountainWest Southern Trails Pipeline Company' remaining only as an inactive/shell FERC certificate holder for already-abandoned mileage), or whether MountainWest retains ownership/FERC-jurisdictional-carrier status while NTUA operates or holds a lesser interest.

Two independent, both-naming sources establish the Owner1 field is at minimum stale, but they point to two different successor entities for two different aspects (corporate-name lineage vs. the operating segment's transfer to a tribal utility). Recommend NOT overwriting Owner1 with a single new value; instead flag as contested/needs-review with both candidate chains documented, and note in ResearcherNotes that a Update-leg pass should pull FERC eLibrary or a current PHMSA operator-of-record filing to resolve which entity (MountainWest Southern Trails Pipeline Company vs. NTUA) is the current FERC-jurisdictional owner of record for the surviving segment.

Three independent origins instead describe a Colorado origin: (1) OSTI/DOE trade-journal abstract (1982): 'the Trailblazer Pipeline Co. 436-mile section from Rockport, Colo. to Beatrice [Neb.]'; (2) Tallgrass's own historical company-overview page (via a 2019-07-27 Wayback snapshot, since the live pipeline.tallgrassenergylp.com is now behind an Incapsula bot-wall for both live and later-dated Wayback crawls): 'Trailblazer Pipeline Company LLC (Trailblazer) is a 436-mile pipeline extending from northeast Colorado to Gage County in Nebraska'; (3) Wikipedia's (en.wikipedia.org, independent of GEM/gem.wiki) 'Trailblazer Pipeline' stub, categorized under 'Natural gas pipelines in Colorado' and 'Natural gas pipelines in Nebraska' (NOT Wyoming), stating plainly it 'brings natural gas from Colorado into Nebraska.' The one source in tension with this is Tallgrass's own 2015 SEC S-1 registration statement, which hedges: 'The Trailblazer Pipeline is a FERC-regulated natural gas pipeline system with approximately 436-miles of transportation pipelines that begins along the border of Wyoming and Colorado and extends to Beatrice, Nebraska' -- consistent with an origin very close to the state line (Cheyenne, WY sits only a few miles north of the CO border; Rockport, CO sits just south of it) but not itself naming Wyoming as the state of origin. Weighing three independent, more specific sources (a contemporaneous trade journal, Tallgrass's own historical company page, and Wikipedia) against one hedged company-filing sentence, Colorado is the better-supported StartState/Province. Not proposing a specific StartLocation replacement (e.g. 'Rockport') given the S-1's own border-region framing and no fully independent second source for that particular place name -- leaving StartLocation as a lower-confidence open question rather than overreaching. EndLocation='Beatrice'/EndState/Province='Nebraska' are NOT contested -- all three of the above sources, plus the S-1, agree on the Nebraska/Beatrice-area terminus (the 2019 Tallgrass page's 'Gage County' is the same place -- Beatrice is the Gage County seat).

concerns.recommendation: clear FuelSource -- 'Colorado' is a state name, not an upstream field/plant/facility, and violates the documented GEM schema convention for this column
concerns.researcher_notes: Per docs/reference/gem_schema.md's explicit documented gotcha, FuelSource (gas sheet) must name the upstream gas source feeding the line -- a specific field, plant, or facility (e.g. 'Abqaiq', 'Berri Gas Plant') -- and must NEVER be a state name or the commodity type. GEM's current value 'Colorado' is a state, not a named field/facility, so it is a schema-convention violation independent of the classification finding above. I could not confidently attribute a single named upstream field: Trailblazer historically received Rocky Mountain/Overthrust-belt gas (per the OSTI/Justia sources on the original three-segment Trailblazer System) via multiple interconnects rather than one dedicated field, and ADM's project-overview map depicts 'Cheyenne Hub' (a well-known multi-source trading/interconnect hub in the DJ Basin straddling the CO/WY line) near the pipeline's origin, but no source I found states outright that Cheyenne Hub (or any other single named point) IS Trailblazer's FuelSource in the GEM sense. Recommending the cell be cleared (left blank) rather than replaced with an unverified guess, per the schema doc's own instruction ('if you can't attribute one, leave it blank and note why -- do not default it'). This is also now moot with respect to the CO2 conversion: whichever way the classification question above is resolved, FuelSource as currently entered is a defect either way.

concerns.recommendation: sharply reduce LengthKnown -- current 1287 km appears to record the Uniontown,PA-to-Kosciusko,MS mainline distance, not the pipe actually built; verify against the FERC CP16-3-000 order/EA before pasting any replacement number
concerns.researcher_notes: MATERIAL SPEC DISAGREEMENT. GEM records LengthKnown=1287.00 km (~800 route-miles), which is roughly the highway/mainline distance between the recorded termini Uniontown, PA and Kosciusko, MS. But TETCO's OWN project page -- the same page that supplies the capacity and in-service-date values above -- describes the actual constructed facilities in one explicit sentence: 'Facilities Shared facilities with Access South and Lebanon Extension: 16 miles of pipeline relay or loop within or adjacent to existing Texas Eastern ROW; Additional compression at existing stations; 3 existing receipt meters converted for bi-directional flow; Various other modifications to existing facilities.' Enbridge's own 2017 SEC 6-K annual report corroborates the SCOPE (not the mileage): 'The facilities for these projects include pipeline looping, as well as modifications and expansions of existing compressor stations on SEP's Texas Eastern pipeline system' -- i.e. this is a looping/compression expansion of an EXISTING mainline corridor, not ~800 miles of new pipe. 16 miles (~25.7 km) is the combined figure for Access South AND Lebanon Extension together, so Access South's own share is some unknown fraction of that -- meaning the true value is almost certainly under 26 km, not 1287 km, an overstatement on the order of 50x. This is the exact 'route/corridor distance vs actual new pipe' confusion the sweep SOP warns about (c.f. Rockies Express Zone 3 in this same roster). I am NOT proposing a specific replacement number because the 16-mile figure is not disaggregated between Access South and Lebanon Extension and I found no second, independent source stating a mileage (FERC eLibrary's docket-sheet UI is a JS single-page app that returns no content to scripted fetches -- CP16-3-000 needs a browser session to pull the actual order/EA PDF, which would very likely state exact looping mileage by segment; the NGI article naming this docket is subscriber-paywalled even via Wayback; SEC full-text search for other shipper filings turned up only capacity/timing, no mileage). Do not paste 0 either -- some new pipe clearly was built, just not 800 miles of it.

concerns.recommendation: Verify the exact current peak-day design capacity before citing a ref for the sheet's 3,120 MMcf/d. Enbridge's own factsheet — the most authoritative source found — states 'peak day capacity: 3.09 Bcf/d' (3,090 MMcf/d), about 1% below the sheet value.
